ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 5 — Annual Wellness Visit, Subsequent — George H. W. Bush

text.paragraph: Subsequent annual wellness visit; no new complaints. [S]

Mr. Bush is a 67-year-old man who returns for his subsequent annual wellness visit five weeks after his four-month review. He had his initial annual wellness visit with his previous primary care clinician last year. Since the spring he has had paroxysmal atrial fibrillation triggered by Graves' disease, treated with radioactive iodine, and is now on levothyroxine for the hypothyroidism that followed. He completed the health risk assessment before the visit. He takes levothyroxine 100 mcg each morning before breakfast, five weeks after the dose was raised, and has missed no doses. Metoprolol and apixaban were stopped at the last visit after a 14-day monitor showed sinus rhythm throughout; he has had no palpitations, lightheadedness, or breathlessness since. He runs three miles four days a week. He has no new concerns. [S]

Voluntary advance care planning discussion of about 20 minutes, with his consent. He named a health care agent, and a health care proxy form was completed; the agent is recorded in the chart and is not named here. He said that what matters most to him is staying active, keeping working, and being told plainly about his health so he can make his own decisions. He chose not to record specific treatment preferences today. The plan will be revisited yearly and with any change in his health. [S]
